title: Opening the Door Without the Key
paragraphs: Psychedelics such as psilocybin, ketamine and LSD are increasingly regarded as remarkably effective treatments for serious mental illness, yet how they work remains unclear. Their benefit might reside in the radical disruption of brain chemistry and neural firing patterns, in the overwhelming experience of the trip, in the therapy that gives it meaning, or in some combination of the three. Most attempts to disentangle these possibilities have so far concentrated on engineering analogues that omit the trip yet, in mice, appear to reproduce some of the drugs' effects on neurons.

A growing minority of neuroscientists, among them Nicco Reggente at the University of California, Los Angeles, are exploring the converse hypothesis: that the therapeutic value derives from an intense alteration of perception, which upends a person's sense of self and of their place in the world. If so, drugs may be dispensable whenever other means can shake up the mental snow globe and let it settle into a healthier arrangement; psychedelics would merely be particularly good at picking the lock of a door that has other keys. Such alternatives have a long pedigree. Holotropic breathwork, a form of deliberate hyperventilation, was devised in the 1970s after psychedelic drugs were outlawed, and meditation and sensory deprivation can also transform mental states. Interest in these methods grew out of the psychedelic research of the 1950s and 1960s, but waned as Prozac and other antidepressants arrived and mental health research moved on.

With many obstacles to the clinical use of psychedelics unresolved, drug-free approaches have returned to the agenda, this time with technology as a central component. The best studied is stroboscopic light stimulation, in which rapidly flashing lights beamed onto closed eyelids generate vivid visual hallucinations within seconds, without the training that meditation or breathing practices require. In a 2024 study of 262 people, the technique reduced anxiety and improved mood as effectively as breath-focused meditation, and did so in just over five minutes rather than ten. One proposed explanation is predictive processing, the theory that the brain builds its picture of the self and the world by generating predictions from past experience and comparing them with incoming sensory information; colours that move in unexpected ways would then undermine the implicit confidence that the world is as it habitually appears, potentially opening the mind to change.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Researchers have shown that brain chemistry is the source of the benefits, because analogues that omit the trip reproduce some of the drugs' effects in mice.
options.explanation: Analoglar ilaçların nöronlar üzerindeki bazı etkilerini taklit eder; metin yararın kaynağının beyin kimyası olduğunu göstermez, mekanizmayı belirsiz bırakır.

options.text: Researchers have shown that therapy is the source of the benefits, because it gives the experience its meaning.
options.explanation: Terapi, olası kaynaklardan (kimya, deneyim, terapi) yalnızca biridir; sorumlu olduğu gösterilmemiştir.

options.text: Researchers have proposed that altered perception is the source of the benefits, which would make drug-free ways of inducing it worth testing.
options.explanation: Reggente gibi araştırmacılar yararın algının yoğun değişiminden geldiğini ileri sürer; bu doğruysa ilaçsız yöntemler (nefes çalışması, ışık uyarımı) sınanabilir.

options.text: Researchers have shown that drug-free methods work better than the drugs, because meditation and breathwork predate the research on psychedelics.
options.explanation: Işık uyarımı meditasyonla karşılaştırılır, ilaçlarla değil; nefes çalışması ise ilaçlar yasaklandıktan sonra, 1970'lerde geliştirildi.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is closest in meaning to 'psychedelics would merely be particularly good at picking the lock of a door that has other keys'?

options.text: Psychedelics are an especially effective but replaceable way of reaching a state that other methods can also produce.
options.explanation: 'Particularly good at picking the lock' etkinliği, 'a door that has other keys' ise aynı duruma başka yollarla da ulaşılabildiğini anlatır.

options.text: Psychedelics are the quickest of several routes to a state that the other methods can only partly approximate.
options.explanation: Hız karşılaştırması yoktur ve diğer yöntemlerin aynı kapıyı açtığı söylenir; yalnızca yaklaştıkları değil.

options.text: Psychedelics are effective only because they open a door that the other methods have already unlocked for them.
options.explanation: Neden-sonuç tersine çevrilir: ilaçlar diğer yöntemlerin açtığı kapıdan yararlanmaz; kapıyı kendileri açar.

options.text: Psychedelics are a forceful but unreliable way of reaching a state that the other methods reach more gently.
options.explanation: 'Picking the lock' kaba kuvvet değil ustalık çağrıştırır; güvenilmezlik ya da diğer yöntemlerin daha yumuşak olduğu söylenmez.

questions.prompt: How does Reggente's hypothesis relate to the approach that most earlier studies have taken?

options.text: It reverses it: most studies keep the drugs' neural effects and drop the experience, while the minority keep the experience and question the drug.
options.explanation: İlk paragraf çoğu çalışmanın deneyimi dışarıda bırakan analoglar kurduğunu, ikinci paragraf azınlığın bunun tersini (deneyimin değeri) denediğini söyler: 'converse'.

options.text: It extends it: both groups try to reproduce the drugs' effects on neurons, but the minority do so with technology rather than with analogues.
options.explanation: Azınlığın hipotezi nöron etkilerini yeniden üretmeye değil, algının yoğun değişiminin yararını sınamaya dayanır.

options.text: It contradicts it: the minority deny that the trip has any therapeutic role and concentrate on therapy as the only active ingredient.
options.explanation: Azınlık, deneyimin (yoğun algı değişimi) tedavi edici olabileceğini savunur; deneyimi reddetmez.

options.text: It confirms it: the minority treat the engineered analogues in mice as proof that altered perception is what drives the benefit.
options.explanation: Analoglar deneyimi atlar; deney farelerde nöron etkilerini taklit eder ve algı hipotezini kanıtlamaz.

questions.prompt: Which of the following conclusions is NOT supported by the final paragraph?

options.text: Flashing lights may produce an effect comparable to that of meditation, and may do so more quickly.
options.explanation: Bu sonuç desteklenir: ışık uyarımı kaygıyı ve ruh halini meditasyon kadar iyileştirir ve bunu yaklaşık yarı sürede yapar.

options.text: The 2024 study found no advantage for meditation over the light technique in reducing anxiety.
options.explanation: Bu sonuç desteklenir: iki yöntem benzer ölçüde etkili bulunur.

options.text: Predictive processing is offered as a possible explanation of the effect, not as an established mechanism.
options.explanation: Bu sonuç desteklenir: 'One proposed explanation' ve 'potentially' ifadeleri açıklamanın kesin olmadığını gösterir.

options.text: The 2024 study showed that flashing lights alter a person's sense of self just as psychedelic drugs do.
options.explanation: Metin yalnızca ışık uyarımının kaygıyı azalttığını ve ruh halini iyileştirdiğini söyler; benlik algısını psikedeliklerle aynı biçimde değiştirdiği gösterilmemiştir.

sources.claim: Psikedeliklerin mekanizması belirsiz; ilaçsız alternatifler (nefes çalışması 1970'ler, meditasyon, duyusal yoksunluk) ve stroboskopik ışık uyarımı; 2024'te 262 kişilik çalışmada meditasyon kadar etkili ve 5 dakikadan biraz fazlada etki; öngörücü işleme açıklaması.
